subs.label: Speculative Series
subs.axis: Axis: by speculative premise — science-fiction premises first (space, aliens, time, technology, society's end), then costumed heroes, then fantasy worlds, then the supernatural among us, then horror; comic and anthology forms at the edges of each run.

leaves.label: Space Opera
leaves.defn: A series whose drama plays out among starships, space stations and interplanetary polities (Star Trek, Babylon 5, The Expanse, The Mandalorian). Earth-bound alien drama goes to B9-2; a comic space series to B9-11.
leaves.see: B9-2 Alien Invasion; B9-11 Comic Science Fiction
leaves.axis: by franchise first, then by mode: Star Trek, Star Wars, Stargate, Battlestar Galactica and military space opera, space westerns and adventure operas, exploration and colony dramas

leaves.label: Alien Invasion
leaves.defn: A series whose engine is extraterrestrials arriving on Earth — as conquerors, hidden infiltrators, first contacts or neighbours (V, Falling Skies, 3 Body Problem, Roswell). Star-faring drama goes to B9-1.
leaves.see: B9-1 Space Opera; B9-22 Occult Detective Fiction
leaves.axis: by the shape of the contact: open invasion, hidden conspiracy, first contact, aliens living among us

leaves.label: Time Travel
leaves.defn: A series whose premise is movement through time — travellers, slips, rewrites or loops (Doctor Who, Quantum Leap, 12 Monkeys, JIN). Time-slip romance with rebirth goes to B9-19.
leaves.see: B9-19 Magic Realism; B9-4 Mystery Box
leaves.axis: by what the traveller does with time: roams it, changes it, slips into the past, repeats a day

leaves.label: Mystery Box
leaves.defn: A serial built on a withheld central enigma that the audience decodes over seasons — an island, a vanished flight, a town no one can leave (Lost, Dark, Manifest, The OA). If the enigma is solved weekly by investigators, B9-22.
leaves.see: B9-3 Time Travel; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Techno-thriller
leaves.defn: A science-fiction thriller whose threat is a near-present technology or experiment — clones, enhancements, fringe science (Orphan Black, Fringe, Limitless, Kyle XY). Machines that think go to B9-6; costumed powers to B9-12.
leaves.see: B9-6 Artificial Intelligence in Fiction; B9-12 Superhero Fiction
leaves.axis: by the technology at stake: genetics and cloning, human enhancement, fringe science and conspiracy

leaves.label: Artificial Intelligence in Fiction
leaves.defn: A series whose premise is a thinking machine or a simulated world — androids, AI, virtual reality, cyberpunk cities (Westworld, Humans, Altered Carbon, Memories of the Alhambra).
leaves.see: B9-5 Techno-thriller; B9-7 Dystopian Fiction
leaves.axis: by where the artificial mind lives: robot bodies, simulated worlds, cyberpunk society

leaves.label: Dystopian Fiction
leaves.defn: A series set in an oppressive engineered society, or a contest that society stages for survival (The Handmaid's Tale, 3%, Severance, Alice in Borderland). A world after a catastrophe goes to B9-9.
leaves.see: B9-9 Apocalyptic & Post-Apocalyptic Fiction; B9-8 Alternate History
leaves.axis: by what oppresses: the state, technology or the corporation, a selection or survival game

leaves.label: Alternate History
leaves.defn: A series set in a history that diverged at a known point (The Man in the High Castle, For All Mankind, SS-GB). A traveller who changes history goes to B9-3.
leaves.see: B9-3 Time Travel; B9-7 Dystopian Fiction

leaves.label: Apocalyptic and Post-Apocalyptic Fiction
leaves.defn: A series about the end of civilisation — the plague, collapse or impact, or the world that survives it (Station Eleven, Jericho, The 100, Fallout). Zombie apocalypses go to B9-28.
leaves.see: B9-28 Zombie Apocalypse; B9-7 Dystopian Fiction
leaves.axis: by the stage of the end: pandemic and extinction, wasteland after collapse, catastrophe still coming

leaves.label: Anthology Series
leaves.defn: A science-fiction or fantasy series telling a self-contained story with new characters each episode (The Twilight Zone, Black Mirror, The Outer Limits, Amazing Stories). Horror anthologies go to B9-26.
leaves.see: B9-26 Horror Anthology

leaves.label: Comic Science Fiction & Comic Fantasy
leaves.defn: A series that plays a science-fiction or fantasy premise chiefly for laughs (Red Dwarf, The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Good Omens, The Watch). A sitcom with a light fantastic touch stays in B8.
leaves.see: B8 Comedy Series; B9-1 Space Opera
leaves.axis: by the premise mocked: science fiction, then fantasy

leaves.label: Superhero Fiction
leaves.defn: A series about costumed or superpowered heroes and their villains (Smallville, Daredevil, The Boys, Moving). Japanese henshin heroes go to B9-13.
leaves.see: B9-13 Tokusatsu; B9-5 Techno-thriller
leaves.axis: by source and tradition: DC Comics, Marvel Comics, creator-owned and original heroes, ensemble superpower dramas, Asian superhero series

leaves.label: Tokusatsu
leaves.defn: A Japanese special-effects hero series built on transformation (henshin), suit actors and miniature monsters, and its adaptations (Kamen Rider, Himitsu Sentai Goranger, Ultraman, Power Rangers).
leaves.see: B9-12 Superhero Fiction; C1 Action & Battle Anime
leaves.axis: by franchise: Super Sentai, Kamen Rider, Ultra Series, Metal Heroes and other henshin heroes, Power Rangers adaptations last

leaves.label: High Fantasy
leaves.defn: A series set wholly in an invented secondary world of magic, kingdoms and quests (Game of Thrones, The Wheel of Time, The Witcher, Alchemy of Souls). Myth and legend retold go to B9-15.
leaves.see: B9-15 Mythic Fiction; B4 Chinese-Language Drama
leaves.axis: by world-building scale: epic invented worlds, East Asian invented worlds, sword-and-sorcery adventure

leaves.label: Mythic Fiction
leaves.defn: A series that retells myth, legend or epic, or brings old gods into the modern world (Hercules: The Legendary Journeys, Merlin, Alif Laila, American Gods).
leaves.see: B9-14 High Fantasy; B9-16 Fairy Tale & Portal Fantasy
leaves.axis: by the mythology drawn on: Greco-Roman, Arthurian and European, Arabian and Asian epics, gods in the modern world

leaves.label: Fairy Tale & Portal Fantasy
leaves.defn: A series that retells fairy tales or sends its characters through a door into a magical land (Once Upon a Time, The 10th Kingdom, His Dark Materials, A Series of Unfortunate Events).
leaves.see: B10 Children's Series; B9-14 High Fantasy
leaves.axis: by the frame: fairy-tale retelling, portal or parallel world, children's literary fantasy

leaves.label: Historical Fantasy
leaves.defn: A period series in which magic or the uncanny is woven into recognisable history (Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell, The Nevers, Carnival Row).
leaves.see: A8 Historical & Period Film; B9-18 Urban Fantasy

leaves.label: Urban Fantasy
leaves.defn: A series in which witches, shapeshifters, fae, angels or demons live hidden in the present-day world (Charmed, Lost Girl, The Magicians, Preacher). Teen-centred versions go to B9-21; investigators of the uncanny to B9-22.
leaves.see: B9-21 Supernatural Teen Drama; B9-22 Occult Detective Fiction
leaves.axis: by the hidden beings: witches, shapeshifters and fae, hidden magical worlds, angels, demons and immortals

leaves.label: Magic Realism
leaves.defn: A realist drama with one impossible premise taken matter-of-factly — a body swap, a second life, a grim reaper at work (Reborn Rich, Dead Like Me, Mystic Pop-up Bar, Wonderfalls). Fully supernatural worlds go to B9-18.
leaves.see: B9-20 Paranormal Romance; B2 Korean Drama
leaves.axis: by the impossible premise: body swap, rebirth and second life, afterlife and fate, other magic-realist dramas

leaves.label: Paranormal Romance
leaves.defn: A romance whose lover is supernatural — a gumiho, ghost, angel or beast (Tale of the Nine-Tailed, Bring It On, Ghost, A Discovery of Witches). Vampire romance goes to B9-23.
leaves.see: B9-23 Vampire Fiction; A13 Romance
leaves.axis: by tradition: Korean fantasy romance, Chinese and Japanese supernatural romance, Western paranormal romance

leaves.label: Supernatural Teen Drama
leaves.defn: A teen drama in which adolescents fight, love or become monsters (Buffy the Vampire Slayer, The Vampire Diaries, Teen Wolf, Stranger Things).
leaves.see: B9-18 Urban Fantasy; B9-23 Vampire Fiction
leaves.axis: by the teens' role: slayers, witches, vampire and werewolf romances, teen horror mysteries

leaves.label: Occult Detective Fiction
leaves.defn: A series of cases solved by investigators of the paranormal — agents, psychics, hunters (The X-Files, Supernatural, Medium, Grimm). A serial enigma with no case-of-the-week goes to B9-4.
leaves.see: B9-4 Mystery Box; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by the investigator: paranormal agents, psychics and mediums, monster hunters and exorcists, supernatural cops and consultants

leaves.label: Vampire Fiction
leaves.defn: A series centred on vampires (Dracula, True Blood, The Strain, Angel). Teen vampire romance goes to B9-21.
leaves.see: B9-21 Supernatural Teen Drama; B9-20 Paranormal Romance
leaves.axis: by the vampire's role: Gothic monster, plague, lover and society, detective or hero

leaves.label: Ghost Story
leaves.defn: A horror series driven by the dead returning to haunt a place, a family or an object (The Haunting of Hill House, Ju-On: Origins, Rose Red, Archive 81).
leaves.see: B9-25 Supernatural Horror; B9-19 Magic Realism
leaves.axis: by what is haunted: houses and Gothic settings, Asian ghost horror, cursed media

leaves.label: Supernatural Horror
leaves.defn: A horror series whose threat is demonic, occult or cosmic (The Exorcist, Midnight Mass, Lovecraft Country, Penny Dreadful). Ghosts go to B9-24; vampires to B9-23.
leaves.aliases: folk horror; religious horror; cosmic horror
leaves.see: B9-24 Ghost Story; B9-26 Horror Anthology
leaves.axis: by the evil's source: demons and religion, cults and folk ritual, the cosmic, Gothic literature

leaves.label: Horror Anthology
leaves.defn: A horror series with new stories by episode or by season (Tales from the Crypt, American Horror Story, Masters of Horror).
leaves.see: B9-10 Anthology Series
leaves.axis: by format: hosted classic anthologies, season-long anthologies, episodic modern anthologies

leaves.label: Slasher
leaves.defn: A horror series in which a killer stalks and picks off a group one by one (Scream: The TV Series, Harper's Island, Chucky).
leaves.see: B9-30 Psychological Horror; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Zombie Apocalypse
leaves.defn: A series about survival among the risen or infected dead (The Walking Dead, All of Us Are Dead, The Last of Us). Non-zombie collapse goes to B9-9.
leaves.see: B9-9 Apocalyptic & Post-Apocalyptic Fiction
leaves.axis: by franchise and tradition: The Walking Dead franchise, other zombie survival, East Asian zombie series

leaves.label: Creature Feature
leaves.defn: A series whose threat or wonder is a monster or prehistoric beast (Primeval, Tremors, Sweet Home, Parasyte: The Grey).
leaves.see: B9-13 Tokusatsu; B9-28 Zombie Apocalypse
leaves.axis: by the creature: dinosaurs and lost worlds, giant monsters and sea creatures, monster-siege survival, body horror and parasites

leaves.label: Psychological Horror
leaves.defn: A horror series whose terror is in minds and violence rather than the supernatural (Hannibal, Servant, Yellowjackets).
leaves.see: B9-27 Slasher; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Comedy Horror
leaves.defn: A horror series played for laughs (Ash vs Evil Dead, The Baby, Post Mortem: No One Dies in Skarnes).
leaves.see: B8 Comedy Series; B9-11 Comic Science Fiction & Comic Fantasy

subs.label: Competition Formats
subs.axis: Axis: by what contestants are judged on — performance first (talent, singing, idol debut), then survival in a social game, then a craft, then knowledge, luck or play.

leaves.label: Talent Show
leaves.defn: A competition in which acts perform before judges or the public (Got Talent, Strictly Come Dancing, RuPaul's Drag Race). Singing-only contests go to B13-2.
leaves.see: B13-2 Singing Competition
leaves.axis: by the act: open variety talent, dance, celebrity performance, comedy, magic and novelty

leaves.label: Singing Competition
leaves.defn: A competition among singers decided by judges or votes (The Voice, Pop Idol, The X Factor, Star Academy). Idol-group debut shows go to B13-3.
leaves.see: B13-3 Idol Survival Show

leaves.label: Idol Survival Show
leaves.defn: A competition in which trainees vie for places in a debuting pop group, or groups battle for rank (Produce 101, Girls Planet 999, Queendom, I-LAND).
leaves.see: B13-2 Singing Competition; B15-2 Real Variety

leaves.label: Reality Competition
leaves.defn: An unscripted contest in which players live, travel or endure under rules and are eliminated until one wins (Survivor, Big Brother, The Amazing Race, Physical: 100).
leaves.see: B14-1 Dating Show; B13-6 Game Show
leaves.axis: by the contest's engine: live-in social elimination, races, physical challenges, strategy games, skill and business contests, comedy endurance

leaves.label: Cooking Competition
leaves.defn: A contest among cooks or bakers (MasterChef, The Great British Bake Off, Iron Chef, Culinary Class Wars). How-to cookery goes to B14-8.
leaves.see: B14-8 Instructional Television

leaves.label: Game Show
leaves.defn: A studio programme in which contestants play a game for prizes (Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, The Price Is Right, Family Feud, Taskmaster). Comedy panel shows go to B15-4.
leaves.see: B15-4 Panel Show; B13-4 Reality Competition
leaves.axis: by the game played: quiz, words and puzzles, panel and guessing, chance and pricing, physical, music, comedy

subs.label: Factual Entertainment Formats
subs.axis: Axis: by the real situation the camera arranges — courtship, everyday lives, an experiment, a transformation, a trick, a ghost hunt, a journey, a lesson, a ruling.

leaves.label: Dating Show
leaves.defn: A programme that sets up real people to date, pair or marry (The Bachelor, Love Is Blind, Single's Inferno, Taken Out).
leaves.see: B13-4 Reality Competition; B5 Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama
leaves.axis: by format: studio dating games, dating reality, same-sex dating reality

leaves.label: Docusoap
leaves.defn: An observational series following real people's lives as ongoing serial drama (The Osbournes, Jersey Shore, Terrace House, Cops).
leaves.see: B11 Documentary Series; B14-3 Social Experiment
leaves.axis: by whose lives are followed: celebrities and families, ensembles in structured reality, people at work

leaves.label: Social Experiment
leaves.defn: A factual format that places people in a contrived situation to see how they cope (Wife Swap, Undercover Boss, 60 Days In, The Rehearsal).
leaves.see: B14-2 Docusoap; B13-4 Reality Competition

leaves.label: Makeover Show
leaves.defn: A format that transforms a person, home or business before the camera (Queer Eye, Extreme Makeover: Home Edition, Supernanny, Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares).
leaves.see: B14-3 Social Experiment
leaves.axis: by what is made over: the person, the property, the troubled life or business

leaves.label: Hidden Camera
leaves.defn: A programme that films unwitting people reacting to staged pranks, or stunts staged for the camera (Candid Camera, Punk'd, Impractical Jokers, Jackass).
leaves.see: B14-3 Social Experiment; B15-1 Variety Show

leaves.label: Paranormal Television
leaves.defn: A factual series investigating hauntings and the unexplained (Ghost Hunters, Paranormal State). Scripted ghost hunters go to B9-22.
leaves.see: B9-22 Occult Detective Fiction

leaves.label: Travel Documentary
leaves.defn: A presenter-led entertainment series built on a journey or road trip (Top Gear, The Grand Tour, Running Wild with Bear Grylls, Conan O'Brien Must Go).
leaves.see: B11 Documentary Series; B15-2 Real Variety

leaves.label: Instructional Television
leaves.defn: A how-to or explainer programme that teaches a skill or tests ideas (The Joy of Painting, Good Eats, MythBusters, Antiques Roadshow).
leaves.see: B13-5 Cooking Competition; B10 Children's Series

leaves.label: Court Show
leaves.defn: A programme in which a television judge arbitrates real small-claims disputes (Judge Judy, Judy Justice).
leaves.see: B14-3 Social Experiment

subs.label: Variety & Talk Formats
subs.axis: Axis: by what the host-led show presents — a revue of acts, cast members at play, conversation, comedy panels, clips, a single performance broadcast.

leaves.label: Variety Show
leaves.defn: A hosted revue of comedy, music and novelty acts (The Ed Sullivan Show, The Red Skelton Show, The Flip Wilson Show, Wetten, dass..?). Korean cast-based variety goes to B15-2.
leaves.see: B15-2 Real Variety; B15-6 Television Special

leaves.label: Real Variety
leaves.defn: A Korean-style variety programme in which a fixed celebrity cast plays missions, travels, runs a business or is observed living (Running Man, New Journey to the West, I Live Alone, Run BTS!).
leaves.see: B15-1 Variety Show; B13-3 Idol Survival Show
leaves.axis: by what the cast does: missions and games, being observed, travel and hospitality, idol-group content

leaves.label: Talk Show
leaves.defn: A host-led programme of conversation with guests or audience (The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson, The Daily Show, The Ellen DeGeneres Show, The Graham Norton Show).
leaves.see: B15-4 Panel Show
leaves.axis: by slot and voice: late-night, satirical news, daytime and tabloid, celebrity chat

leaves.label: Panel Show
leaves.defn: A comedy programme in which a panel of comedians plays a loose quiz or improvisation game (Have I Got News for You, QI, Whose Line Is It Anyway?). Prize-driven games go to B13-6.
leaves.see: B13-6 Game Show; B15-3 Talk Show
leaves.axis: by the game: topical news quiz, comedy panel game, improvisation

leaves.label: Clip Show
leaves.defn: A hosted programme built from home videos or viral clips (America's Funniest Home Videos, Ridiculousness, Tosh.0).
leaves.see: B15-1 Variety Show

leaves.label: Television Special
leaves.defn: A broadcast of a single performance — concert, opera, stage relay or stand-up set (MTV Unplugged, Austin City Limits, Great Performances, James Acaster: Repertoire).
leaves.see: A14 Musical & Dance Film; B15-1 Variety Show
